The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the term “EC2” – that’s Amazon Web Services.  
> * The RTX A6000 is available only on certain machine types (e.g., `n1-standard-8`, `n1-highmem-8`, etc.).  
> * You must have the **Compute Engine API** enabled and the **GPU quota** granted for your project.  
> * The instance must be created in a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports GPUs
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # or any machine type that supports GPUs
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE",count="$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --boot-disk-device-name="$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Picks the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a script on first boot. |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access. |

> **Tip**: If you need more than one GPU, increase `GPU_COUNT` and adjust the machine type accordingly (e.g., `n1-standard-16` for 2 GPUs).

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

You can also call the Compute Engine REST API directly. Below is a sample `POST` request body you would send to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
```

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### How to send the request

1. **Authenticate**: Use OAuth 2.0 to obtain an access token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute`.
2. **Make the POST**: Include the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header and send the JSON body above to the URL:
   ```
   https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/instances
   ```

> **Note**: Replace `your-project-id` and `us-central1-a` with your actual project ID and zone. Adjust the `machineType` and `acceleratorType` URLs if you choose a different zone or machine type.

---

## Quick Checklist

- [ ] **GPU quota**: Verify you have a quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in the chosen zone.  
- [ ] **Billing enabled**: GPU instances incur additional costs.  
- [ ] **Firewall rules**: The tags `http-server` and `https-server` automatically open ports 80 and 443.  
- [ ] **Driver installation**: The startup script installs the NVIDIA driver; you may need to adjust the driver version.  

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine ubuntu@<external-ip>
nvidia-smi
```

That should show the RTX A6000 GPU and its status. Happy computing!
